t.1.71.1: When the king of Videha had spoken thus, the great sage Viśvāmitra, together with Vasiṣṭha, addressed these words to that heroic king.
t.1.71.2: O best of men, the lineages of the Ikṣvākus and the Videhas are inconceivable and immeasurable; there is no one equal to them.
t.1.71.3: O king, the righteous alliance of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa is fitting, and fitting too in its wealth of beauty, with Sītā together with Ūrmilā.
t.1.71.5: This is King Kuśadhvaja, the younger brother, a knower of dharma. O king, O best of men, we ask for the two daughters of this righteous-souled one, unequalled in beauty on earth, to be wives.
t.1.71.4: It is not for you to speak, O best of men; let my words be heard.
t.1.71.7: These sons of Daśaratha, endowed with beauty and youth, are all like the guardians of the worlds, with valor equal to that of the gods.
t.1.71.6: O king, we would ask for your two daughters, those noble-souled maidens, as brides for prince Bharata and the wise Śatrughna.
t.1.71.8: O lord of kings, let your steadfast Ikṣvāku family, you whose deeds are meritorious, be bound to us by the alliance between us both.
t.1.71.9: Having heard Viśvāmitra's words, with Vasiṣṭha in agreement, Janaka then, with joined palms, spoke these words to the two bulls among sages.
t.1.71.11: O great sage, on a single day let the four mighty princes take the hands of the four princesses.
t.1.71.10: This alliance of our families, which you two yourselves command, is fitting. So be it, and blessings upon you all: let Śatrughna and Bharata, both together, take these two daughters of Kuśadhvaja as their wives.
t.1.71.13: Having spoken these gentle words, King Janaka rose to greet them and, with palms joined in reverence, addressed both of the eminent sages.
t.1.71.12: On the day that follows the Phalgunīs, O brahman, under the asterism where Bhaga is the presiding lord, the wise commend the marriage rite.
t.1.71.14: Supreme dharma has been accomplished for me; I am ever the disciple of you both. Let the two foremost of sages be seated on these choicest seats.
t.1.71.16: When Janaka of Videha had spoken thus, King Daśaratha, the delight of the Raghus, was overjoyed and replied to that lord of the earth.
t.1.71.15: Just as this city belongs to Daśaratha, so too the city of Ayodhyā is mine; there was never any doubt about this lordship. You two should do what is fitting.
t.1.71.17: You two brothers, lords of Mithilā, are endowed with countless virtues; the sages and the assemblies of kings have been duly honored by you both.
t.1.71.18: "May you attain well-being; good fortune be with you! I shall go to my own abode and perform all the śrāddha rites," he said.
t.1.71.19: Then the greatly renowned King Daśaratha, having taken leave of that lord of men, placed those two foremost of sages before him and went away quickly.
t.1.71.21: In accordance with dharma, the king, lord of men, gave to the brāhmaṇas hundreds of thousands of cows for each of his sons, dedicating them to each son in turn.
t.1.71.20: Having gone to his lodging, the king performed the śrāddha according to the prescribed rule; then, rising early at daybreak, he made an excellent gift of cows.
t.1.71.22: Four hundred thousand cows, their horns adorned with gold, well-endowed, each with its calf and with milking pails of bronze, did that bull among men bestow.
t.1.71.23: Raghunandana, devoted to his sons, also gave the twice-born a great deal of other wealth, offering it for the godāna rite of his sons.
t.1.71.24: Then that king, surrounded by his sons who had performed the gift of cows, shone like the gentle Prajāpati surrounded by the guardians of the worlds.
